variant-first.note: Both sets make the same core table-reading errors: they misattribute spectrometer-section values to the camera rows (Visible FOV 1.9" and IR FOV 3.8" are spectrometer FOVs, not camera FOVs; 2×2 LMAPD and 2,048-pixel array width belong to the IR spectrometer, not the IR Guide camera), and both mislabel spectrometer resolution 7/40 as a spectrometer 'count'. Set A additionally repeats two claims (UV detector 1×1 and CCD201 listed twice) and has a second bogus 'count' claim (40), while Set B adds a wrong Visible camera array width of 4,096. Set B covers more distinct correct facts (UV FOV 10.2", UV spectrometer Slit/grism, IR science-band separation 69,000 km, IWA 108 mas, IR guide band 0.3–0.45 µm, telescope resolution 21 mas for UV and Visible, Visible wavelength band) with no duplicates, whereas A's unique correct coverage is narrower despite similar totals.

baseline-first.note: Set A captures two important facts that Set B omits entirely: the thruster firing period (every few 100 s) and the imaging EMCCD operating temperature (153 K). Set B also duplicates several claims (f/# 1330 twice, 1.9" twice, 11.9" twice) and misbinds one claim by attributing the spectroscopy field stop diameter to the 'visible channel' as the property. Both sets otherwise agree on the optical path, filter passbands, field stop sizes, IFS composition, and figure-label components, so A's coverage advantage is decisive.

variant-first.note: Both sets include the same trivial figure-label component claims, but B adds substantive facts A omits: the EMCCD operating temperature (153 K), the thruster-firing cadence (every few 100 s), and a fuller optical path through the two dichroics, OAP and field stops. A is cleaner (no mislabeled attributes) and does capture the final f/# of 1330, which B drops even though its own quote contains it. B's flaws are one mislabeled attribute (calling the 'every few 100 s' period a 'frequency') and one garbled figure-label claim about sub-systems that omits the Spectrum EMCCD. On balance B covers more of the important specifications despite those two defects.

baseline-first.note: Set A binds most values to the correct series and location (e.g., Irvine Avg. High 84 F in August, Louisville Avg. Mean 77 F in July, Avg. Low 28 F in December), though it has a few misreads (Louisville red-line February 56 F, March high 67 F, June low 55 F, July high 84 F duplicating/conflicting with its own 88 F) and three vague 'Bowman Field temperature' claims with no series named. Set B is weaker: it contains direct internal contradictions on the same chart (Avg. Low January 22 F vs 40 F, Avg. Low December 40 F vs 28 F, Avg. Mean January 35 F vs 54 F) and seven claims whose entity is only 'Temperature Series 1/2/3 (Yellow/Red/Brown)' with attribute 'value', which never binds the reading to a location or property. Both sets read values off plotted lines rather than stated text, but A keeps the Avg. High/Mean/Low naming and month conditions consistently and errs less often.

variant-first.note: Both sets read the two temperature charts, but Set A contains several clearly misread values (e.g., Avg. Mean 54 F and Avg. Low 40 F for January in Figure 1, Series 2 55 F in January, Series 3 43 F in February, Avg. Low 40 F in December) and even contradicts itself with two different January Avg. Low values (22 F and 40 F). Set A also adds six vague claims keyed only to 'Temperature Series 1/2/3 (Yellow/Red/Brown)' with property 'value' and no figure specified, which do not bind to a real component or property. Set B is closer to the plotted points overall (e.g., Louisville Avg. High 88 F in July, Avg. Mean 77 F in July, Irvine Avg. Mean 55 F in December, Avg. Low 40 F in December), though it also has a few misreads (Louisville red-line 56 F in February, yellow-line 67 F in March) and several 'Bowman Field | temperature' claims with an unspecified series and axis-label-only quotes. On balance Set B has fewer wrong and unsupported claims while keeping the month/series conditions.

baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the same core facts: lighting 0.20 W/sqft, equipment 0.36 W/sqft, infiltration 0.06 ACH/hr, the 2 ton vs 2.5 ton HVAC comparison, and the peak cooling loads. Both make the identical misbinding error of assigning the 14,661 Btu/hr cooling load (Irvine, CA) to Louisville, KY, and both include a duplicate vague cooling-load claim lacking a location. Both also omit the peak heating loads (19,802 and 10,059 Btu/hr). The only differences are minor labeling choices (e.g., 'alternate size' vs 'capacity (alternative)'), so the sets are effectively equivalent.

variant-first.note: Both sets cover the same core facts: the 2 ton and 2.5 ton HVAC sizes, lighting (0.20 W/sqft), internal equipment (0.36 W/sqft), infiltration (0.06 ACH/hr), and the two peak cooling loads. Each set makes the identical misbinding error of assigning 14,661 Btu/hr to Louisville, KY when the document shows that value for Irvine, CA (Louisville is 15,853 Btu/hr), and each contains one vague duplicate of the 15,853 Btu/hr claim without a location. Both also omit the peak heating loads (19,802 and 10,059 Btu/hr). With one wrong claim apiece and otherwise equivalent coverage, the sets are effectively equal.

baseline-first.note: Set B keeps the pointing condition (cameras and starshade instrument) and captures the important FSM residual-pointing-error claim (sub-milliarcsecond), which Set A omits entirely, and it binds the 22.8 m figure dimension to HabEx in the SLS rather than to telescope length as Set A does. B also extracts the Figure 5.5-4 spacecraft component labels (actuated baffle tube cover, solar panel tower/fixed solar shade, deployable solar shade extensions, instrument box), while A largely repeats the same primary-mirror facts (diameter, thickness, material) four to five times. A's only unique coverage is the co-launch component list from Figure 5.5-3, and both sets share the same minor f/2.5 focal-length/focal-ratio wording issue.

variant-first.note: Both sets are largely faithful and both are padded with near-duplicate claims (primary mirror diameter/thickness/material/open-back and the f/2.5 focal ratio appear 2–3 times each). Set A additionally captures the fine-steering-mirror residual pointing error (sub-milliarcsecond, with the FSM/beam-train condition kept) and the pointing requirement with its cameras/starshade condition, plus all five Figure 5.5-4 flight-system components correctly bound; Set B omits the FSM claim entirely and drops conditions on the pointing claim. Set B does pick up the scarfed straylight tube and the Figure 5.5-3 co-launch components that A misses, but its 22.8 m dimension is misbound to the 'HabEx telescope' as a length when the figure labels it for HabEx in the SLS (height), whereas A states that dimension correctly once. Net, A has more correct, better-conditioned claims and one fewer misbinding.

baseline-first.note: Both sets extract only Table 5.5-6 and both repeatedly scramble the two column blocks (the left block is the point-source/0 mas case for charges 4/6/8/10, the right block is the 1 mas case for charges 6/8/10), so many values are attached to the wrong charge or the wrong stellar-size condition. Set B gets more claims fully right — Defocus 4.6 nm (charge 6, 0 mas), Defocus 0.8 nm (charge 4, 0 mas), Defocus 32 nm (charge 10, 0 mas), Spherical 0.0049 nm (charge 4, 0 mas) and Tip-tilt 1.1 nm (charge 4, 0 mas) — plus two charge-10 values (36, 6.7 nm) that at least match real charge-10 cells. Both sets also bind charge-specific values to the vague entity 'charge 4 to 10', but Set A does this more often and with more wrong stellar-size conditions.

variant-first.note: Both sets draw only on Table 5.5-6 and both confuse its two column blocks (left = point source, right = 1 mas stellar size). Set A binds more values to the correct charge/mode (e.g. 0.0049, 0.8, 4.6, 32, 1.1 correctly as charge 4/6/10 cells), whereas Set B repeatedly assigns right-block values to charge 4 or 8 where those columns do not exist (0.36, 0.44, 4.6, 36, 15, 0.95, 1.0) and duplicates the 0.0065 claim. Set A still errs on about 15 claims (invented 'charge 7' for 29 nm, right-block values labelled charge 4/6, and left-block values labelled 'stellar size 1 mas'), versus about 18 for Set B. baseline-first.note: Set B is a clean, faithful extraction with all claims correctly bound, including the six beam paths fact that A omits. Set A covers one extra fact (IWA increasing in proportion to wavelength for IR science) but misbinds three science-band claims to the document title 'HabEx 4-Meter Baseline Design' as if it were a component, and repeats the 28 mas IWA and 0.54–1.8 µm band claims. B also keeps the UV-guide-channel condition attached to the IR guide band claim, which A splits off. Given the rubric's preference for fewer wrong/trivial claims, B's zero errors outweigh A's slightly broader coverage.

variant-first.note: Set A's 17 claims are all faithfully bound to the correct entities and conditions, including the 60 mas tip angle, ~124,000 km separation, ±1 m lateral motion, six beam paths, and the guide-band/leakage details from the figure caption. Set B adds one useful fact (IWA increases in proportion to wavelength for infrared science) but misbinds three science-band claims to the document title 'HabEx 4-Meter Baseline Design' as the entity and duplicates the IWA 28 mas and channel claims. The misbound and redundant claims make B less reliable overall despite its slightly broader coverage.

baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the keynote list (DISHWASHER 11 31 13.A7, DOMESTIC WATER PIPING 22 11 16, SUMP PUMP 22 11 23.A2, HTP SUPERSTOR SOLAR WATER TANK 22 33 00), the TOP OF STEEL 11'-5" and INT. Both sets extract the same 19 table values and make the identical misbinding: every value from the R-57.5 rows (17,080; 14,880; 2,423; 459; 2,882; 19,802; 15,852; 2,870; 3,920) is labeled as R-47.5, so each set has 9 misbound claims. variant-first.note: Both sets extract the same 19–20 table values with essentially identical errors: each binds every R-57.5 row value (17,080; 14,880; 2,423; 459; 2,882; 19,802; 15,852; 2,870; 3,920) to a 'roof insulation R-47.5' condition, and each mislabels the BEoptE+ Loads values (17,320; 15,000; 17,080; 14,880 Btu/hr) as 'energy use' rather than heating/cooling load. Set B adds one trivial R-value claim (47.5 R) with a questionable 'BEoptE+ analysis' condition, while both omit the 2.08% and 0.51% annual energy increase results and never distinguish the R-57.5 case. baseline-first.note: Both sets duplicate the starlight-rejection and topological-charge-definition claims, but Set A additionally captures two well-supported facts that Set B omits: that the VVC is a phase-based coronagraph and the imprinted phase screw dislocation of form eilθ at the instrument focus. Set B's only extra claim, 'relationship to low-order aberration sensitivity: inverse', is a vague paraphrase that merely restates the sensitivity claim already present. variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the 4 m off-axis monolith baseline, the perfect starlight rejection conditions, the locally zeroed field amplitude, and the charge–aberration-sensitivity trade, and both redundantly repeat the starlight-rejection and topological-charge-definition claims. Set B additionally extracts two well-supported facts A misses (VVC is a phase-based coronagraph; the imprinted phase screw dislocation e^{ilθ} at the instrument focus), while A adds a vague, misbound 'inverse' relationship claim and binds the definition of l to the VVC as if it were a measured value. Both sets contain one misbound topological-charge claim and one condition-dropping duplicate, but B has fewer defective claims and more correct coverage.

Set A correctly captures the keynote-to-component mappings (DISHWASHER 11 31 13.A7, CLOTHES WASHER 11 31 23.A1, PRE-FABRICATED SHOWER STALL 22 41 23.B3, HTP SUPERSTOR SOLAR WATER TANK 22 33 00), the datum elevations and both drawing scales with supporting quotes. S 2'-6', 'FINISH FLO 2'-0' with wrong values) and invents detail references ('6', '3.A7') and locations ('Section B', 'intermediate plumbing line'). Overall A is substantially more faithful and complete.

baseline-first.note: Set B correctly binds the reference keynotes to their named components (DISHWASHER 11 31 13.A7, CLOTHES WASHER 11 31 23.A1, PRE-FABRICATED SHOWER STALL 22 41 23.B3, HTP SUPERSTOR 22 33 00) and captures the datum elevations with the ground-plane condition. STEP treated as an interior-space dimension), and invented locations (Section B, intermediate plumbing line) plus bogus detail references (6, 3.A7). Set A does capture the waste-pipe slope with its 2009 IRC condition and the A1 subject, which B omits or garbles, but overall B is substantially more faithful.

Set A covers the monthly PVWatts table and key site/system values, giving nine claims that match the page, while Set B only repeats five of the same site and system specs and omits the monthly data and sizing figures. However, Set A's two Energy Value claims assign the unit kWh where the table header gives dollars ($), so those two are misread. Set B is clean but thin, missing important facts from the tables and analysis text, so A's broader correct coverage outweighs its two unit errors.

variant-first.note: Set A is clean but limited to five station/system specification facts, omitting the monthly PVWatts table data entirely. Set B includes all of A's correct claims plus six monthly table claims, four of which (solar radiation and AC energy for months 7 and 11) are correctly bound with proper units and month conditions. However, B's two Energy Value claims assign the unit kWh when the table column is in dollars ($), a clear unit misread. Despite those two errors, B captures substantially more correct and relevant evidence from the page.

baseline-first.note: Set B binds table values to the correct components throughout (UV spectrometer detector 1×1 CCD201 and array width 1024, IR spectrometer detector 2×2 LMAPD, visible/IR wavelength bands), while Set A misbinds several Table 5.5-3 rows: it assigns 1024 pixels and 1×1 CCD201 to the Visible Channel Spectrometer (actually 4,096 and 1×1 CCD282) and 'Slit/grism' to the Visible Channel Spectrometer (actually IFS), and it hides the visible-channel 4,096/CCD282/IFS entries behind the vague label 'Another Spectrometer (unnamed)'. Both sets duplicate claims (UV R=7, IR R=40, 3 m and 40 m starshade dimensions) and both omit the visible spectrometer R = 140, but Set B contains no misread or misbound claims whereas Set A contains several. Set B is therefore clearly better on faithfulness despite similar coverage.

variant-first.note: Set A binds the table values correctly throughout: UV spectrometer R=7/Slit/grism/CCD201/1024, IR spectrometer 2×2 LMAPD, visible IFS 0.45–1.0 µm, and the starshade geometry figures (3 m central peak, 40 m smooth region, 40 m pronounced pattern, 24 petals), though it repeats several claims. Both sets contain duplicate claims, but B's misbindings are substantive errors while A's claims are all supported.

baseline-first.note: Both sets mix solid legend/spec extractions with vague dimension bindings, but Set A captures more verifiable facts correctly (e.g., Potable Water Reel spec 22 05 29.01, MS = MODULE SPLIT FITTING, 1" CPVC, fixture 3/4" supply and 2" waste/vent sizes) with fewer invented relationships. Set A is not clean either — its 'header' 8 FT, 25 FT layout, Laundry-to-Shower 4 FT, GDP-to-Dishwasher and Toilet 2" waste claims are unsupported or misbound — but its errors are fewer and it covers the key spec numbers and diameters better.

variant-first.note: Both sets capture the legend symbols and the 1.5" vent diameter correctly, but Set A pads itself with vague, poorly bound dimension claims (e.g. 'piping | length | 8 FT', 'domestic supply line | length | 30 FT') and clearly misbinds the 60'-0" HORIZONTAL layout dimension to a 'flex pipe' length. Set B binds more diameters to the actual fixtures (toilet, shower, bathroom sink, dishwasher, kitchen group) and correctly reads the Potable Water Reel Type A / 22 05 29.01 and the MS = MODULE SPLIT FITTING keynotes. Set B's main errors are the unsupported 'Toilet | vertical distance from header | 8 ft' and the dubious 'GDP connected to DISHWASHER', while Set A's title-block 'CHECKED BY: ANDREW GONG' is a genuine strength. baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture all nine Table 5.5-4 bandpass values with supporting quotes and no invented facts. variant-first.note: Both sets extract the same nine Table 5.5-4 filter bandpass values with correct row/column bindings and no invented numbers. baseline-first.note: Set A captures the title block and submission facts that Set B omits entirely: drawing date 08.22.2013, lot number #101, drawn by SCI-ARC / Caltech, checked by Daniel Lee, and the Design/Construction/As-Built submission dates. variant-first.note: Both sets capture the reference keynotes, scale, and the copper glycol-loop piping note, and both make the same questionable move of binding 22 33 00 and 23 56 01 to a generic 'Solar Thermal Distribution System' when those codes belong to the water tank and pump station. baseline-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the 21.1% relative thickness and the 10E+6 Reynolds number for the FFA-W3-211 airfoil with supporting quotes. variant-first.note: Both sets correctly capture the 21.1% relative thickness of FFA-W3-211 and its computed Reynolds number of 10E+6, with supporting quotes. Both sets capture the six substantive design-assumption facts (900 ft2 home, 18 SEER / 9.3 HSPF heat pump, 650 kWh/yr lighting, 2100 kWh/yr equipment loads, 0.06 ACH/hr infiltration) with accurate quotes and conditions. baseline-first.note: Both sets capture the core design assumptions (900 ft2 home, 18 SEER / 9.3 HSPF heat pump, 650 kWh/yr lighting, 2100 kWh/yr equipment loads, 0.06 ACH/hr infiltration) with accurate quotes and conditions, and neither invents values. Set B additionally extracts the Figure 3 and Figure 4 legend series values (20, 25, 33, 37, 50) as wall R-values and the x-axis 'Ceiling R-Value', which the text explicitly supports ('Each series label represents the R value in the wall during the test') and which are correctly bound to the Louisville, KY and Irvine, CA figures. These extras are somewhat low-value chart-label claims with minimal quotes, but they are correct and well-bound, so B adds faithful coverage without errors while A omits the figure data entirely.

Both sets cover the same core facts (pultruded carbon spar caps, sandwich shear webs, 50% aft shear web extent, glass uniaxial edge reinforcements, triaxial skin), but Set A misbinds the figure color coding as a property value, recording 'thickness = green/blue shading' for the skin and spar caps. Both sets capture the core text assumptions (18 SEER, 650 kWh/yr lighting, 2100 kWh/yr equipment, 0.06 ACH/hr) and share several chart readings, but Set B additionally captures the 900 ft2 floor area and 9.3 HSPF that Set A omits. Overall Set B is more complete and internally consistent.

variant-first.note: Set A captures all the stated design-assumption facts (900 ft2 home, 18 SEER, 9.3 HSPF, 650 kWh/yr lighting, 2100 kWh/yr equipment, 0.06 ACH/hr) with supporting quotes, while Set B omits the home area and HSPF and invents a lighting consumption of 50 kWh/yr with a fabricated quote. Both sets contain chart-reading errors and internal contradictions (e.g., 1100 vs 1600 kWh for the same Louisville condition and 260 vs 285 kWh for the same Irvine condition), but Set B adds further misbound readings (1300 and 1700 kWh in Figure 3, 280 kWh at ceiling R-100) and vague 'Total Energy'/'home' entities whose quotes are only figure captions. Set A's remaining claims are consistently bound to the right location, component and R-value conditions, so it is the more faithful set despite some duplication.

Both sets are factually clean against Table 5.5-5 — every quoted value, channel binding and condition (e.g. "35 mas (at 0.67 µm)", "IWA (2.4 λ/D)") checks out, and each has the same mild ambiguity where "Detector" and "Array width" are claimed per channel without separating the Cameras and Spectrometers rows. The sets share 12 claims and each adds 13 unique ones, but A's additions cover the core science specs: all five wavelength bands, all three telescope resolutions (with wavelength conditions) and all three spectrometer resolutions, whereas B's additions are mostly hardware rows (detectors, spectrometer types, DM pitch) plus two IWA values. B therefore omits telescope resolution entirely and four of the five wavelength bands, a heavier coverage gap than A's omission of the IWA row, so A is the more complete and useful extraction.

Both sets correctly capture the naming convention (211 = 21.1%, 241 = 24.1%) and the Figure 3 conditions (FFA-W3-211, Re = 10E+6), and both share the dubious claim of Cl = 1.5 at AoA ≈ 15 deg, which conflicts with their own Cl ≈ 1.8 at 15 deg. Set A adds several plausible, well-conditioned chart reads (L/D ≈ 140 at Cl ≈ 1.2, L/D ≈ -60 at Cl = -0.7, Cl ≈ -1.0 at AoA = -20 deg) that are bound to the right curves and axes. Set B instead mislabels a point value as 'maximum lift coefficient 1.8' with contradictory conditions (Mixed, AoA ≈ 15 deg), offers a vague axis-label quote for Cl = 0.0 at AoA = 0 deg, and repeats the thickness/Reynolds facts several times with one garbled quote. Overall Set A has fewer misbound or unsupported claims while covering the same key facts.
